title: Touring Europe with the kids' band
summary: He names the countries visited and describes the regional feel of pre-war Europe.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: One question about that, it says in Chilton's book that you travelled extensively throughout Europe.
That's when you were doing the French Line?
Switzerland, France, Germany, England; that was it. We didn't get down into Italy. We had to do it between trips.
Did you see or hear anything notable?

Only collecting an ambiance, certainly a feeling and I get that feeling every time I listen to Stravinsky of that period or Ravel in that period. It doesn't take too much imagination to go back a few years and catch Debussy either. It had a different feeling than it does today. New York had a different feeling. How do you describe that? I don't know. Europe was always a difficult place, I'm sure it was, but it also had more peripheral dimensions than it does now. It was impersonal, but not so impersonal. There were regionalisms; France was very definitely French. You don't any longer feel that. Britain was an island and there were walls around that island. When you entered the place you felt you were entering a medieval castle.
You almost think of Europe as an entity anymore.
They were locked in, local, regional cultures. And that's what gave them their tastes, their flavor. It was true in this country too.
